STANDING HEXAGRAM NAME AND PRONUNCIATION:

[Traditional Chinese]

  艮（ㄍㄣˋ）

[Simplified Chinese]

  艮（gèn）

[English, Wilhelm-Baynes]

  Kên / Keeping Still, Mountain

[English, James Legge]

  LII. The Kăn Hexagram


LINES:
(One moving line)

[Traditional Chinese]

  (Scripture)
  六五：艮其輔，言有序，悔亡。

  (Exegesis)
  艮其輔，以中正也。

[Simplified Chinese]

  (Scripture)
  六五：艮其辅，言有序，悔亡。

  (Exegesis)
  艮其辅，以中正也。

[English, Wilhelm-Baynes]

  (Scripture)
  Six in the fifth place means:
  Keeping his jaws still.
  The words have order.
  Remorse disappears.

  (Exegesis)
  Six in the fifth place:
  a) Keeping his jaws still.
  The words have order.
  Remorse disappears.
  b) “Keeping his jaws still,” as a result of central and correct behavior.

[English, James Legge]

  (Scripture)
  5. The fifth SIX, divided, shows its subject keeping his jawbones at rest, so that his words are (all) orderly. Occasion for repentance will disappear.

  (Exegesis)
  5. 'He keeps his cheek bones at rest:'--in harmony with his central position he acts correctly.


EMERGING HEXAGRAM 53:

(Line at bottom is first)

  7  ━━━━━━━━━  （六, 6th）──┐
  7  ━━━━━━━━━  （五, 5th）──┼── 風（上卦）
  8  ━━━   ━━━  （四, 4th）──┘   wind, wood (upper trigram)
  7  ━━━━━━━━━  （三, 3rd）──┐
  8  ━━━   ━━━  （二, 2nd）──┼── 山（下卦）
  8  ━━━   ━━━  （初, 1st）──┘   mountain (lower trigram)

(First is line at bottom)

  8, 8, 7, 8, 7, 7

EMERGING HEXAGRAM NAME AND PRONUNCIATION:

[Traditional Chinese]

  漸（ㄐㄧㄢˋ）

[Simplified Chinese]

  渐（jiàn）

[English, Wilhelm-Baynes]

  Chien / Development (Gradual Progress)

[English, James Legge]

  LIII. The Kien Hexagram


LINES:
[Traditional Chinese]

  (Scripture)
  漸：女歸吉，利貞。

  (Exegesis)
  山上有木，漸；君子以居賢德，善俗。

[Simplified Chinese]

  (Scripture)
  渐：女归吉，利贞。

  (Exegesis)
  山上有木，渐；君子以居贤德，善俗。

[English, Wilhelm-Baynes]

  (Scripture)
  DEVELOPMENT. The maiden
  Is given in marriage.
  Good fortune.
  Perseverance furthers.

  (Exegesis)
  On the mountain, a tree:
  The image of DEVELOPMENT.
  Thus the superior man abides in dignity and virtue,
  In order to improve the mores.

[English, James Legge]

  (Scripture)
  Kien suggests to us the marriage of a young lady, and the good fortune (attending it). There will be advantage in being firm and correct.

  (Exegesis)
  LIII. (The trigram representing) a mountain and above it that for a tree form Kien. The superior man, in accordance with this, attains to and maintains his extraordinary virtue, and makes the manners of the people good.
